about-p1: Tokadai Code Club is a free coding club for children aged 7–17. Participants called "Ninjas" build websites, games, and apps on their own.
about-p2: There is no fixed curriculum. Learn Scratch, HTML/CSS, JavaScript, Python, or whatever you like at your own pace. Volunteer mentors are here to think alongside you and offer support.
about-p3: We hope to be a place where children in the Tokadai area (Komaki East, Kasugai, Kozoji) discover the joy of making things and expand their possibilities for the future.
ninja-p: Participants are called "Ninjas". Wield code as your weapon and create projects that are uniquely yours!
features-desc: From your very first line of code to full-scale app development. A place where every child can shine.
feat1-p: No participation fees whatsoever. We provide an environment where kids can learn programming for free.
feat2-p: No fixed curriculum. Decide what you want to do and move at your own speed. Beginners and advanced learners are all welcome!
feat3-p: Experienced volunteer mentors think through problems alongside you. Rather than teaching, they help you "discover" together.
feat4-p: Meet peers who share your interests. Work on projects as a team, share ideas, and grow your circle of friends.
feat5-p: Based in Tokadai, we continue activities for local children. Engineers who will fly from Tokadai to the world!
feat6-p: We regularly hold showcases to present work. Showing what you made to others sparks motivation for your next creation.
cta-p: Ninjas (7–17) and Mentors alike — come join us in Tokadai!
footer-desc: A coding club for children in the Tokadai area (Komaki East, Kasugai, Kozoji) to discover the joy of creating through code.
footer-copyright: © 2026 桃花台コードクラブ (Tokadai). Powered by volunteers. 🌸

venue-soon-sub: The venue is confirmed! Sessions will be held at Komaki City East Citizens Center, 2F Study Room.
venue-access-desc: Accessible on foot or by bus from the Tokadai area.
venue-bus-p: Use Meitetsu Bus, Aoi Kotsu Peach Bus / Tokadai Bus, or Komaki City Community Bus "Komakuru". A short walk from the nearest stop. Check Google Maps for details.
venue-car-p: Parking is available. Detailed parking information will be provided after the venue is confirmed.
venue-walk-p: The venue is accessible on foot or by bicycle from the surrounding area. Bicycle parking is also available.
venue-about-p1: Tokadai is a large-scale new town in eastern Komaki City, Aichi Prefecture, developed from the 1970s. True to its name meaning "peach blossom terrace," beautiful flowers bloom in spring.
venue-about-p2: The town is home to a diverse mix of residents — families, seniors, singles, and young people. Tokadai Code Club aims to serve as a bridge, fostering cross-generational connections in this community.
venue-about-p3: From this town where lush parks and high-rise apartments coexist, we aim to be a place where people of all ages can expand their possibilities through the power of digital technology.
venue-cta-p: Observers are welcome too. Feel free to get in touch anytime.
news-page-desc: Event schedules, activity reports, mentor recruitment, and more.
mentor-desc: A volunteer role you can start from just 2 hours. Anyone aged 18+ (student or professional) is welcome. Pass on the joy of programming to the next generation.
mentor-why-desc: It's not just about contributing to children — there's plenty that comes back to you as an engineer.
mentor-why1-p: A child's simple question — "Why does it work this way?" — hits your own blind spots. You'll sharpen your ability to put the essence of technology into words.
mentor-why2-p: You can directly take part in nurturing the next generation of engineers right in your local community of Tokadai. It gives you a real sense of giving back.
mentor-why3-p: You naturally connect with mentors from different industries and technical backgrounds. Job-hunting tips, side projects, and study groups naturally arise.
mentor-why4-h3: Kids' "I did it!" is the best feeling
mentor-why4-p: The look on a child's face the first time their code runs is priceless. Pure joy you rarely experience in day-to-day work.
mentor-why5-p: Activities are just a Sunday afternoon for 2 hours. Even busy professionals can keep it up. If you need to skip a month, just let us know in advance.
mentor-why6-p: Sustained volunteer work can go in your portfolio or resume. A great way to demonstrate character and social awareness when job-hunting.
contact-page-desc: Whether you want to join, observe, volunteer as a mentor, or help as a supporter — feel free to reach out.
contact-welcome-p: First-timers, observers, parents with questions, or anyone interested in volunteering as a mentor — all enquiries are welcome!

event-desc: Held on a Sunday for 2 hours. Registration via connpass is required.
volunteer-desc: We are looking for people to support children's learning. Two participation styles: "Mentor" for technical guidance, and "Supporter" for event operations.
volunteer-banner-p: Two ways to get involved: Mentor (technical guidance) or Supporter (event operations). No programming experience needed for supporters!
volunteer-mentor-p: Use your programming skills to support Ninjas in their projects. You can join from just 2 hours.
volunteer-supporter-p: Help with reception, setup, and photography. No programming experience required.
curr-h2:
Choose What You Love
from a Rich Menu
curr-desc: No fixed curriculum. Choose any topic that interests you and challenge yourself at your own pace.
curr-scratch-p: A visual programming language ideal for beginners — combine blocks to create games and animations.
curr-text-p: Build apps, games, and automation tools with real programming languages.
curr-web-p: Start with HTML & CSS and build your own website or portfolio.
curr-video-p: Shoot and edit on your phone or PC. Learn to create short videos and content for YouTube and social media.
curr-ai-p: Try "Vibe Coding" — the next-gen skill for building apps at lightning speed by working with AI.
also-desc: Beyond programming, you can explore making, design, and content creation.
also-hw-p: Control LEDs and sensors using Raspberry Pi and electronics kits. Get a taste of IoT and embedded development by programming a robot yourself.
also-design-p: Using Canva and STUDIO, go from design basics to publishing a website without code. Sharpen your sense of design while bringing ideas to life.
also-sns-p: Learn branding, content strategy, and analytics tools to boost your own and the dojo's online presence.
curr-note: These are just examples. If you think "I want to try that!", go for it! Expand your possibilities together with a mentor.
news1-p: Tokadai Code Club is preparing to launch in summer 2026 or later. Sessions are planned on a Sunday for 2 hours. The venue — a public facility in eastern Komaki — is being coordinated. Updates will be posted here and on social media once details are confirmed.
news2-p: Tokadai Code Club is recruiting mentors to support the children. Please lend your skills in Scratch, JavaScript, Python, PHP, Web development, video production, AI development (Claude Code / Vibe Coding), Web design (Canva · STUDIO), electronics (Raspberry Pi · kits · embedded), SNS management, or anything else you are good at. Any age or profession is welcome as long as you have programming experience. It's a volunteer role from a Sunday afternoon for 2 hours.
news3-h3: Tokadai Code Club Official Website Launched
news3-p: The official Tokadai Code Club website is now live. Find the latest session info, curriculum details, and mentor recruitment here. The site works great on smartphones too. Tokadai is home to a diverse community — families, seniors, singles, and more — and we aim to be a Dojo open to everyone.
news-cta-p: First-timers very welcome. Observers welcome too!
supporter-desc: Mentors provide technical guidance to Ninjas; Supporters handle event operations. Both roles are essential to the Dojo.
supporter-mentor-desc: Use your programming knowledge to support Ninjas as they build their projects. The style is thinking alongside them, not lecturing.
supporter-mentor-li1: Those with programming or technical knowledge
supporter-mentor-li2: Those who want to think through code with Ninjas
supporter-mentor-li3: Those who want to witness children's "I did it!" moments
supporter-main-desc: No programming knowledge required. You help run the event — reception, venue setup, and recording activities. Supporters are the backbone behind the scenes.
supporter-note: 💡 Supporters focus on operational assistance, so no programming experience is needed at all. Whether you love the Dojo atmosphere or simply want to contribute to your community, you are very welcome.
mentor-looking-desc: No specific language or credential required. We welcome those who love programming and enjoy working with children.
mentor-ok1: Students or working adults aged 18+University students, vocational students, adults — all welcome
mentor-ok2: Someone with programming experienceAny language, any number of years, even as a hobby — OK
mentor-ok3: Those with engineering experienceSoftware, application, systems, hardware, mechanical engineers — all fields welcome
mentor-ok4: Researchers or technologists outside the IT industryManufacturing, agriculture, healthcare — any field is welcome
mentor-ok5: Those with parenting experienceSupport from a parent's perspective is a great strength
mentor-ok6: Those who've "never taught children before"Starting out just by supporting other mentors is perfectly fine
mentor-ok7: Those who may have sessions they can't attendThere's no obligation to attend every time

mentor-no2: Teaching experience or tutoring experienceThe style is "thinking together" rather than "teaching"
mentor-no3: A specific language or skill setYou adapt flexibly to the interests of the Ninjas you support
mentor-no4: Preparation time or prior studyThere's no curriculum, so you can handle things on the spot on the day
mentor-style-p:
💡 Tokadai Code Club Mentor Style
Rather than giving answers, you ask questions to help Ninjas "discover" the answer themselves. So what matters more than perfect knowledge is the attitude of saying "Let's look it up together."
mentor-flow-desc: A Sunday afternoon for 2 hours. That's your time as a mentor.
mentor-tl1-p: Mentors share information with each other. Check who is participating today and review the previous session. Orientation for first-time mentors happens here.
mentor-tl2-p: Ninjas (children) arrive one by one. Those attending for the first time get a careful explanation. Everyone takes a seat freely and work begins.
mentor-tl3-p: Ninjas work on their individual projects. Mentors reach out to children who are struggling, think alongside them, and support them in expanding their ideas.
mentor-tl4-p: Ninjas who wish to show what they made today present to everyone. Presenting is not compulsory.
mentor-tl5-p: After the Ninjas leave, mentors do a brief reflection together. Share anything notable and notes for next time, then wrap up. Great work today!
mentor-faq1-q: QWhat skills do I need to become a mentor?
mentor-faq1-a: No specific language or skill is required. Ninjas work on a wide range of topics including Scratch, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, Python, electronics, and robot programming. Having an area you're good at is enough. For areas you don't know, "let's look it up together" is perfectly fine.
mentor-faq2-q: QIs it OK if there are months I can't attend?
mentor-faq2-a: No problem at all. Just let us know in advance if work or family circumstances prevent you from attending. There's no obligation to attend every month — just keep going at a sustainable pace.
mentor-faq3-q: QWhat should I do at my first mentor session?
mentor-faq3-a: For your first session, just moving alongside an experienced mentor is perfectly fine. For the first few sessions, it's OK to just "watch, listen, and help a little." The way to move around naturally becomes clear as you get used to it.
mentor-faq4-q: QAre there any travel expenses or compensation?
mentor-faq4-a: Our club is run on a volunteer basis, so there is no compensation or travel expense reimbursement. However, light refreshments may be provided on occasion.
mentor-faq5-a: No worries! Kids in our club are often focused on programming, so you can naturally connect by "thinking through code together." There's no need to hype them up or take the lead.
mentor-faq6-a: Of course. We also welcome observation visits for those who want to "get a feel for the atmosphere first." Feel free to contact us via the form below.
mentor-apply-h2: Join Us in Building the Dojo! 🌸
mentor-apply-p: Observation and trial participation are very welcome. Feel free to send us a message first. Our team will get back to you.

faq-desc: Here are answers to frequently asked questions. If your question isn't answered, feel free to contact us.
faq1-a: Participation is completely free. We provide an environment where all children can learn programming at no cost. There are no material or venue fees either.
faq2-q: QCan I join even without programming experience?
faq2-a: Of course! We especially welcome first-timers. Mentors will support you carefully, so even those who aren't comfortable with keyboards can join with confidence. Come and experience the joy of creating something with a computer!
faq3-q: QIs a parent or guardian required to accompany the child?
faq3-a: Children under 12 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian. Parents and guardians are welcome to observe or participate in the Dojo. Children aged 12 and over may attend on their own (please let us know in advance).
faq4-q: QDo I need to bring a laptop?
faq4-a: Please bring a laptop if you have one. Venue computers may be available if there is extra capacity, but this cannot be guaranteed, so we recommend bringing your own if possible. Tablets can also be used for some activities.
faq5-a: There is no fixed curriculum. You can freely choose any topic that interests you. Examples include: Scratch, text programming (JavaScript / PHP / Python), website creation, video production, electronics (Raspberry Pi · kits · embedded development), web design (Canva · STUDIO), social media management, and intro to AI (Claude Code · Vibe Coding). If you think "I want to try that!", anything goes. Mentors will think alongside you and offer support.
faq6-q: QDo I have to attend every time?
faq6-a: Attendance is optional and there is no obligation to come every session. Just join in the months that work for you. However, as there is a venue capacity, please register in advance for the months you plan to attend.
faq7-q: QI'd like to join as a mentor — how?
faq7-a: You're very welcome! Any age or profession is welcome as long as you have programming experience. It's a Sunday afternoon for 2 hours, and no special qualifications are needed. Please support the children in your area of expertise — Scratch, JavaScript, PHP, Python, video production, electronics (Raspberry Pi · embedded development), web design (Canva · STUDIO), intro to AI, and more. Select 'Mentor Application' in the contact form and reach out.
